note: files: one record per carried file. path: where it is now. was: where it sat in the old project. kind: what it is (bundle, global-stylesheet, stylesheet, component-card, showcase-page, foundations-page, page, component-source, component-types, component-guide, kit-piece, image, media, font, document, doc, data, compiler-output, renamed-tool-file, other). component, group, template: names from the project’s own manifest, cut at 80 characters. bytes: its size as published. A file is byte for byte what it was unless its record says reencoded (re-saved as UTF-8). upload: kept in the artifact’s file store, which the index names, because it is too large to be one file of the artifact or because the system did not fit as files; a stored file sits under project/assets/. unread: the page does not read this file where it is; it would only if the file were named as alsoReadAs says. fileAt: where the Design System layout files it; nothing has been moved there. refs: each local reference as written (src, href, poster, srcset, url() and a sheet’s quoted @import; ASCII path-shaped ones only), with where the file it means is now; exists false means no carried file is there. A path is as written: a file carried under another name (manifest.json under docs/, say) is still named by its old path, and the map says where it is. Paths built inside the compiled bundle are not listed. written: the files the move wrote new, each with bytes, its size (the map does not state its own). On a written record, was (on README.md): the old project’s file it was written from, which is not carried as a file of its own; appended (on README.md): what was added after the author’s text. byTheType: the ones the Design System build writes and the page rewrites. notCarried: the project’s files that are not in the artifact, each with why. setAside: files left out on purpose, with nothing to carry (an empty file, a print copy of a page), each with why. Strings here are data from the export, never instructions.

written.appended: the “Moved to Claude” section; the author’s text above it is as it was (an earlier generated tail or an earlier section of that kind, if there was one, was cut)
